independent_reasoning_steps: Apply BASE two-spoke-three-contacts sections1-5 to X itself with z=s. This maps finite simple induced-C5 disk, X own minimality, unique complete-degree5 s, all other effective complete degrees4, sole connected C, three distinct original contacts, two retained differently beta-colored spokes, nonempty R_C and exact complementary F_C.

BASE section5 removes the printed adjacent-spoke requirement. One global permutation names the two actual spoke colors0,1 and their complements2,3; no boundary positions or pieces are independently normalized. The proof is row-local and requires no second rejected row, T4, full B-touch of X, or singleton aligned to U shield midpoint.

Pinning either complementary color gives uncolorable degree-lists on the identical C; Lemma7 forces tightness. Contacts cannot have boundary colors among those complements, so the difference of the two full lists is supported exactly on the three original contacts.

Theorem10 gives block palettes on the same actual blocks. Leaf-block private vertices make block-incidence columns linearly independent. Active blocks exchange the two complementary colors; contact active-degree1 and other active-degree0/2 yield one active incidence tree with three leaves, hence exactly one triangle and three bridge arms of arbitrary and possibly zero length.

Each active triangle vertex has complete degree4 in X; two triangle edges plus first arm edge (or original s-contact for a zero arm) leave one actual extra edge. It is a boundary attachment or an inactive-branch bridge. Block-cut tree structure prevents rejoining and makes distinct branches disjoint; all s contacts are already in the active structure.

If an inactive branch has no actual X boundary attachment, removing it gives one strict-slack vertex in connected C minus that branch. Color that remainder. The branch has no boundary or s pins and its bridge-entry vertex has degree3 inside the branch, so a four-color slack coloring exists; a single whole-branch color permutation makes the bridge proper. This contradicts the rejected pin. Thus all three actual tethers exist in X.

Original bags Z={s}, V_i=triangle vertex plus its complete original arm, O=whole original B plus tether interiors are connected, pairwise disjoint and nonempty. Triangle edges give3 V_i-V_j adjacencies, original contacts give3 Z-V_i, actual tethers give3 V_i-O, and a retained s-spoke gives Z-O. All10 adjacencies are X original edges; e is unused. Zero arms retain the actual contact edge. K5 minor contradicts the restricted disk embedding.
